scenes.headline: How fifteen projects put a typed classifier to work
scenes.sub: Nine days of real code against Jev, read from the source, not the README.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sparkle! Nine days after Jev launched, at least fifteen independent projects had shipped code against it. They all do the same thing.

scenes.text: A cheap, fast, typed classifier sits in front of something slower, riskier or more expensive, and code keeps every threshold and every side effect.
scenes.say: A cheap, typed classifier sits in front of something slower or pricier, and code keeps every threshold and side effect.

scenes.title: Three typed questions, nothing generated
scenes.say: Each project asks one of three typed questions.

items.say: Noul asks yes or no, and returns one probability.

items.text: Score: a place on a rubric
items.say: Score picks a place on a rubric, given as an ordered list, because position is the rubric.
Choice picks one label from a map.

scenes.title: The shape every project converged on

steps.say: Something arrives: a browser step, a log line, a diff. Code narrows it to a short menu.
Jev picks from that menu, with probabilities. What happens next is decided in code, not in the model.
Code acts on it: take the step, skip the log line, or hand the turn to a bigger model.

scenes.label: per decision than Claude Opus 5, for a Mac agent on the same screenshot
scenes.note: 0.13–0.38 s against 5.2 s; date parsing had to be rebuilt in code
scenes.say: On a Mac, three Choice questions cost a hundred and fifty-five times less per decision than Claude Opus 5. But reasoning gets rebuilt in code.

scenes.title: Checking the confidence: one temperature
scenes.say: One open reimplementation asked: do the probabilities mean what they say?

parts.note: one scalar, fit on a separate validation split
parts.say: It fits one temperature, two point three five, on a separate validation split.

parts.note: same winner, softer probability: ECE 7.3% to 2.2%
parts.say: Dividing logits by it can't change the winner, only the sharpness. Calibration error fell from seven point three to two point two percent.

parts.note: one knob, seven dials: severity went from 3.8% to 12.6%
parts.say: But one knob turns seven dials. On the severity task, calibration got worse.

scenes.text: The value is latency and cost in one narrow slot, with code holding the thresholds. Not general intelligence wearing a faster hat.
scenes.say: The value is latency and cost in one narrow slot. Not general intelligence wearing a faster hat.

recap: Three typed questions: Noul, Score, Choice
A cheap classifier in front of something expensive
Temperature scaling gave the first checkable calibration
scenes.say: To recap: typed questions, a cheap classifier up front, and a calibration number you can check.
